builds.title: Human Review Design Framework
builds.final: A HUMAN IS A CONTROL ONLY IF THEY CAN CHANGE THE OUTCOME.

scenes.headline: HUMAN IN THE LOOP?
scenes.body: That phrase hides the part that matters.

scenes.headline: WHEN DO THEY SEE IT?
scenes.body: Before the decision, while it can still change—not after the consequence.

scenes.headline: WHAT CAN THEY SEE?
scenes.body: Evidence, uncertainty, alternatives and what the system actually did.

scenes.headline: WHAT CAN THEY DO?
scenes.body: Approve is not enough. Change, stop, escalate and record must be real powers.

scenes.headline: TIMING · EVIDENCE · AUTHORITY · ESCALATION · RECORD
scenes.body: Human presence becomes meaningful only when these controls work together.

scenes.headline: DESIGN THE REVIEW, NOT THE LABEL.
scenes.body: Test whether the reviewer can actually change or stop the outcome.

builds.title: Multi-Audience Meaning Architecture
builds.final: CHANGE THE LANGUAGE. KEEP THE TRUTH ANCHORED.

scenes.headline: ONE IDEA. MANY AUDIENCES.
scenes.body: Adaptation is useful only if the factual core survives.

scenes.headline: LOCK WHAT MUST NOT MOVE.
scenes.body: Numbers · names · uncertainty · negation · material facts.

scenes.headline: CHANGE THE EXPLANATION.
scenes.body: Register, context, examples and vocabulary may move for the audience.

scenes.headline: CHECK DRIFT SEPARATELY.
scenes.body: Fluency is not evidence that a rewrite preserved meaning.

scenes.headline: AN ANCHOR CHECK IS AN ALARM—NOT PROOF.
scenes.body: Consequential multilingual or domain communication still requires competent review.

scenes.headline: TRUTH FIRST. AUDIENCE SECOND. VERIFY THIRD.
scenes.body: Never let the rewrite become its own source of truth.

builds.title: Unserved Decision Discovery
builds.final: MORE INFORMATION DOES NOT FIX A MISSING DECISION SYSTEM.

scenes.headline: THEY HAVE INFORMATION.
scenes.body: But they still cannot reliably decide what to do.

scenes.headline: THE UNRESOLVED DECISION.
scenes.body: Name the recurring choice—not the content category around it.

scenes.headline: RECURRENCE · CONSEQUENCE · AMBIGUITY · FRAGMENTATION
scenes.body: Four signals make the missing decision structure inspectable.

scenes.headline: A SCORE IS NOT DEMAND.
scenes.body: It does not prove willingness to pay, product-market fit or solution correctness.

scenes.headline: BUILD THE DECISION PATH.
scenes.body: Turn scattered information into an accountable way to choose and act.

scenes.headline: FIND THE DECISION PEOPLE STILL CANNOT MAKE.
scenes.body: Then investigate whether a system—not more content—is what is missing.

builds.title: Manual Intelligence Engine
builds.final: AUTOMATE THE METHOD ONLY AFTER YOU CAN SEE THE METHOD.

scenes.headline: A PILE OF SOURCES IS NOT INTELLIGENCE.
scenes.body: The transformation happens through explicit gates.

scenes.headline: REGISTER THE SOURCE.
scenes.body: Issuer · version · source date · checked date · exact locator.

scenes.headline: SOURCE ≠ ANALYST CLAIM.
scenes.body: Interpretation gets its own object instead of silently inheriting provenance.

scenes.headline: UNVERIFIED STAYS OUT.
scenes.body: Verified requires a note; contradiction and uncertainty remain visible.

scenes.headline: SYNTHESIS FOLLOWS STATUS.
scenes.body: The brief cannot quietly promote unchecked assertions into findings.

scenes.headline: COLLECT → SEPARATE → VERIFY → BRIEF
scenes.body: Make the research method inspectable before automating any part of it.

builds.title: Service-to-Software Discovery
builds.final: MAP THE WORK BEFORE YOU AUTOMATE IT.

scenes.headline: DON’T AUTOMATE THE SERVICE.
scenes.body: Separate the steps first.

scenes.headline: THREE FUTURES.
scenes.body: AUTOMATE · KEEP HUMAN · REMOVE

scenes.headline: LOW-VALUE REPETITION FIRST.
scenes.body: Do not automate waste just because it repeats.

scenes.headline: PROTECT JUDGMENT.
scenes.body: High consequence, ambiguity and exception-heavy work can remain human-led.

scenes.headline: PROTOTYPE STABLE RULES.
scenes.body: Automation is a candidate disposition—not a deployment approval.

scenes.headline: SOFTWARE / HUMAN / GONE
scenes.body: A better workflow can contain all three.

builds.title: Does This Actually Deserve to Be Software?
builds.final: BUILD THE FORM THE PROBLEM EARNS.

scenes.headline: SOFTWARE IS NOT THE DEFAULT.
scenes.body: It is one form the problem may—or may not—earn.

scenes.headline: FIVE POSSIBLE FORMS.
scenes.body: SOFTWARE · SERVICE · DATASET · COMPANY · KEEP SIMPLE

scenes.headline: VALUE · BUYER · ADVANTAGE · MAINTENANCE
scenes.body: Then inspect judgment, durable data and scale.

scenes.headline: THE FORM SHOULD MOVE.
scenes.body: More expert judgment can point to service. Durable evidence can point to dataset.

scenes.headline: IS NOT MORE TECH.
scenes.body: It is the strongest appropriate system the problem can justify.

scenes.headline: KEEP SIMPLE IS A VALID RESULT.
scenes.body: A sophisticated evaluation can conclude that software is unnecessary.

builds.title: Feedback Loop Product Architecture
builds.final: A PRODUCT LEARNS ONLY WHEN FEEDBACK CAN RESPONSIBLY CHANGE IT.

scenes.headline: THE PRODUCT SHIPS.
scenes.body: But shipping is one-way. Collection alone does not make a product learn.

scenes.headline: HEAR FOUR DIFFERENT SIGNALS.
scenes.body: USE · OUTCOME · CORRECTION · UNMET NEED

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · CONSENT · CONSEQUENCE · OWNER
scenes.body: Urgent corrections enter human triage before the ordinary request queue.

scenes.headline: EVIDENCE · AUTHORITY · CAPACITY · ESCALATION
scenes.body: A person in the loop matters only if they can pause, change, record and escalate.

scenes.headline: CHANGE → VALIDATE → COMMUNICATE → MONITOR
scenes.body: The product learns when a bounded improvement safely returns to observed outcomes.

scenes.headline: COLLECTION IS NOT LEARNING.
scenes.body: Design the accountable path by which feedback can responsibly change the product.

builds.title: Decision-Ready Dashboard Standard
builds.final: DATA BECOMES USEFUL WHEN SOMEONE CAN DECIDE AND ACT.

scenes.headline: A WALL OF CHARTS.
scenes.body: More information is visible. The decision is still missing.

scenes.headline: NAME THE DECISION.
scenes.body: Every retained metric must explain how it can change that decision.

scenes.headline: SOURCE · FRESHNESS · COMPARISON · UNCERTAINTY
scenes.body: A highlighted number without context is not yet decision-ready.

scenes.headline: DECISION → OWNER → ACTION → NEXT STATE
scenes.body: Add trigger, deadline, authority and escalation.

scenes.headline: CONFLICTS NEED A PERSON.
scenes.body: The dashboard can expose a conflict. An accountable human must resolve it.

scenes.headline: DATA IS NOT A DECISION.
scenes.body: Build the accountable path from evidence to action and observable change.

builds.title: Place-Sensitive Technology Readiness
builds.final: TRANSFERABILITY IS A PLACE QUESTION.

scenes.headline: IT WORKED SOMEWHERE ELSE.
scenes.body: That does not mean it can work here.

scenes.headline: WHAT MUST THIS PLACE DECIDE?
scenes.body: Keep the recurring decision gap visible before scoring fit.

scenes.headline: NETWORK · POWER · ACCESS · SUPPORT
scenes.body: Add hazards, governance, data, maintenance, and community authority.

scenes.headline: CAPACITY IS NOT AN ASSUMPTION.
scenes.body: Name the local source, owner, gap, and mitigation.

scenes.headline: PILOT · FALLBACK · STOP · AUTHORITY
scenes.body: A high score permits only a controlled local test.

scenes.headline: CHANGE THE PLACE. THE ANSWER SHOULD MOVE.
scenes.body: Transferability is not a property of the technology alone.

builds.title: Give the Idea a Skeleton
builds.final: IF THE IDEA HAS NO STRUCTURE, IT CANNOT BE TESTED.

scenes.headline: THE IDEA SOUNDS CLEAR.
scenes.body: Until two people mean different things by the same noun.

scenes.headline: ENTITIES NEED STABLE IDENTITIES.
scenes.body: A Place is not a Project. A Decision is not a Source.

scenes.headline: TYPE · REQUIRED · CONSTRAINT
scenes.body: Every field earns a meaning and a rule.

scenes.headline: FROM · RELATIONSHIP · TO
scenes.body: Cardinality makes vague connections testable.

scenes.headline: AUTHORITY · LOCATOR · FRESHNESS
scenes.body: Source rules belong in the skeleton—not as cleanup later.

scenes.headline: STRUCTURE IS NOT TRUTH.
scenes.body: It makes assumptions visible enough to validate, challenge, and improve.

builds.title: Entity / Ownership Resolution X-Ray
builds.final: SAME NAME IS NOT THE SAME ENTITY.

scenes.headline: THE RECORDS LOOK THE SAME.
scenes.body: Similarity is a clue—not identity.

scenes.headline: WHAT KIND OF THING IS THIS?
scenes.body: A valid entity model comes before matching.

scenes.headline: IDENTIFIER · ATTRIBUTE · RELATIONSHIP
scenes.body: Every signal carries evidence and source authority.

scenes.headline: CONTRADICTION CAN SPLIT THE RECORDS.
scenes.body: An authoritative mismatch must not disappear into an average.

scenes.headline: REVIEW · RATIONALE · ROLLBACK
scenes.body: The score never executes the merge.

scenes.headline: MINIMIZE BEFORE YOU MATCH.
scenes.body: Use only the attributes necessary to distinguish records in context.

builds.title: AI Use Consequence & Control Mapper
builds.final: CONTROLS SHOULD FOLLOW CONSEQUENCE.

scenes.headline: THE MODEL IS NOT THE USE.
scenes.body: The same capability can carry radically different consequences in different contexts.

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · PEOPLE · DECISION
scenes.body: Classify what the system will actually do—and who can be affected.

scenes.headline: SEVERITY · SCALE · RIGHTS · REVERSIBILITY
scenes.body: Add vulnerability, autonomy, essential services, data sensitivity, and uncertainty.

scenes.headline: OWNER · TEST · MONITOR · APPEAL
scenes.body: Higher consequence earns stronger authority, stop, incident, notice, and record controls.

scenes.headline: CHANGE · PAUSE · CONTEST · REMEDY
scenes.body: A reviewer matters only when those powers are real.

scenes.headline: A SCORE NEVER APPROVES DEPLOYMENT.
scenes.body: Use the map to expose missing architecture—and escalate when consequence outruns control.

builds.title: AI Workflow Consequence Scanner
builds.final: FOLLOW THE CONSEQUENCE THROUGH THE WORK.

scenes.headline: THE MODEL IS ONE STAGE.
scenes.body: Consequence is produced by the full workflow around it.

scenes.headline: INTAKE → DATA → MODEL → DECISION → ACTION
scenes.body: Add monitoring because the workflow does not end when an action ships.

scenes.headline: WHERE DOES IT ENTER?
scenes.body: Incorrect data, automation bias, and failed notice begin at different stages.

scenes.headline: WHAT CAN IT REACH?
scenes.body: A missing control becomes a condition inherited by downstream work.

scenes.headline: OWNER · CONTROL · STOP · MONITOR
scenes.body: Every handoff needs accountable power—not a generic assurance statement.

scenes.headline: FOLLOW THE CONSEQUENCE THROUGH THE WORK.
scenes.body: A propagation score exposes gaps. It never approves deployment.

builds.title: Legal Judgment Architecture
builds.final: RESPONSIBILITY DOES NOT MOVE WITH THE TEXT.

scenes.headline: THE TOOL PRODUCED AN ANSWER.
scenes.body: That does not tell you who researched, interpreted, inferred, decided, or approved.

scenes.headline: RESEARCH · INTERPRETATION · INFERENCE
scenes.body: Each layer needs sources, supervision, authority, and a record.

scenes.headline: STRATEGY · ADVICE · APPROVAL
scenes.body: Professional judgment remains owned by the responsible lawyer.

scenes.headline: THE CLIENT STILL DECIDES.
scenes.body: Objectives and choices allocated to the client are not tool decisions.

scenes.headline: REVIEW · CHANGE · STOP · RECORD
scenes.body: A label is not control unless the lawyer can actually change the outcome.

scenes.headline: RESPONSIBILITY DOES NOT MOVE WITH THE TEXT.
scenes.body: Applicable jurisdictional rules and competent supervising counsel control.

builds.title: Consequence-Aware Escalation Router
builds.final: ESCALATION IS A CHAIN OF AUTHORITY, EVIDENCE, TIME, AND RECOURSE.

scenes.headline: 100 ALERTS ≠ 100 INCIDENTS.
scenes.body: Repeated signals can describe one consequential event—not one hundred separate interruptions.

scenes.headline: GROUP THE EVIDENCE FIRST.
scenes.body: Shared keys collapse repeated signals while preserving every source and state.

scenes.headline: SCORE CONSEQUENCE TRANSPARENTLY.
scenes.body: Severity, scale, rights, reversibility, evidence, and inherited friction remain inspectable.

scenes.headline: AUTHORITY BEFORE AVAILABILITY.
scenes.body: Notify only an authorized owner through a compatible channel, with the reason visible.

scenes.headline: MISSED CLOCK → NAMED BACKUP.
scenes.body: A recorded acknowledgement stops the timeout; otherwise a validated backup receives the chain.

scenes.headline: AUTHORITY · EVIDENCE · TIME · RECOURSE
scenes.body: Escalation is an accountable chain—not a louder notification.

builds.title: Decision Evidence Ledger
builds.final: AN ACCOUNTABLE DECISION REMAINS RECONSTRUCTABLE AFTER THE MOMENT HAS PASSED.

scenes.headline: A DECISION IS NOT A SNAPSHOT.
scenes.body: Accountability requires the actor, authority, time, evidence, alternatives, acknowledgement, result, and corrections.

scenes.headline: LINK THE COMPLETE RECORD.
scenes.body: Open one decision into a temporal chain instead of leaving its rationale scattered.

scenes.headline: REMOVAL MUST EXPOSE THE GAP.
scenes.body: A ledger should show when supporting evidence is missing—not silently preserve a false sense of completeness.

scenes.headline: APPEND. SUPERSEDE. NEVER ERASE.
scenes.body: Corrections preserve the earlier record, the change, its author, its time, and its reason.

scenes.headline: PROVENANCE ≠ PROOF.
scenes.body: A complete sequence does not prove truth, causation, legal authority, compliance, or a correct decision.

scenes.headline: KEEP THE WHO · WHAT · WHEN · WHY
scenes.body: An accountable decision remains reconstructable after the moment has passed.

builds.title: AI Vendor Claim / Procurement X-Ray
builds.final: BUY THE EVIDENCE—NOT THE ADJECTIVE.

scenes.headline: THE CLAIM SOUNDS CERTAIN.
scenes.body: Procurement still needs to know what the evidence can actually support.

scenes.headline: PROMISE ≠ EVIDENCE
scenes.body: Record the vendor claim separately from the artifact offered to substantiate it.

scenes.headline: SCOPE · DATE · METHOD · OWNER
scenes.body: Ask whether the evidence covers this product, this use, this version, and this consequence.

scenes.headline: NAME THE FAILURE PATH.
scenes.body: A control is incomplete without an authorized owner, trigger, response, and retained record.

scenes.headline: SUPPORTED · PARTIAL · UNVERIFIED · CONTRADICTED
scenes.body: Nonbinary findings preserve uncertainty and identify the next verification action.

scenes.headline: BUY THE EVIDENCE—NOT THE ADJECTIVE.
scenes.body: A defensible procurement decision keeps claim, proof, control, and recourse inspectable.

builds.title: Consent & Data Rights Manager

scenes.headline: BUNDLED CONSENT HIDES THE DEAL
scenes.body: A single yes cannot show purpose, data, recipient, retention, reuse, or withdrawal.

scenes.headline: SEPARATE EVERY PURPOSE
scenes.body: Each purpose needs its own scope, permission state, evidence, and decision history.

scenes.headline: EVENTS MUST TELL THE TRUTH
scenes.body: Grant and withdrawal records must form a valid, chronological, append-only state chain.

scenes.headline: WITHDRAWAL CHANGES WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
scenes.body: It stops future consent-based processing without erasing prior facts or overriding lawful obligations.

scenes.headline: ROUTE EVERY RIGHTS REQUEST
scenes.body: Access, correction, deletion, retention, withdrawal, and reuse need an owner, deadline, status, and escalation.

scenes.headline: CONTROL REQUIRES A LIVING RECORD
scenes.body: Consent is specific, changeable, evidenced, and never the only possible legal basis.

builds.final: CONSENT IS SPECIFIC, CHANGEABLE, EVIDENCED, AND NEVER THE ONLY POSSIBLE LEGAL BASIS.

builds.title: Privacy & Data Minimization Engine
builds.final: THE BEST DATA RISK IS DATA NEVER COLLECTED.

scenes.headline: MORE DATA IS NOT MORE INTELLIGENCE
scenes.body: Every collected field creates exposure, retention work, access pathways, and eventual deletion duties.

scenes.headline: START WITH PURPOSE
scenes.body: Name the decision each field supports. Permission does not make unnecessary collection necessary.

scenes.headline: TEST EVERY FIELD
scenes.body: NECESSARY · OPTIONAL · SENSITIVE · DERIVED · PROHIBITED — keep the reason and evidence visible.

scenes.headline: MINIMIZE BEFORE COLLECTION
scenes.body: Remove prohibited fields. Default optional fields off. Replace sensitive detail with the least revealing form.

scenes.headline: DESIGN THE EXIT
scenes.body: Assign retention, deletion, redaction, and downstream handling before the data enters the workflow.

scenes.headline: THE SAFEST DATA HAS NO BREACH PATH
scenes.body: THE BEST DATA RISK IS DATA NEVER COLLECTED.

builds.title: AI Implementation Readiness X-Ray
builds.final: READINESS IS THE ABILITY TO OPERATE THE CONTROLS—NOT THE DESIRE TO DEPLOY.

scenes.headline: A USE CASE IS NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION PLAN
scenes.body: A promising capability can still outrun the organization expected to operate it.

scenes.headline: START WITH WHO CAN BE AFFECTED
scenes.body: Severity, rights, reversibility, scale, and uncertainty determine how much readiness is required.

scenes.headline: TRACE THE REAL WORK
scenes.body: Map intake, data, model, review, decision, action, monitoring, and every accountable handoff.

scenes.headline: TEST THE VENDOR CLAIMS
scenes.body: A procurement adjective is not proof. Keep claim, scope, evidence, control, contract, and recourse inspectable.

scenes.headline: OWNER · AUTHORITY · SKILL · TIME · EXIT
scenes.body: A control exists only when named people can run it, stop the use, correct failure, and sustain the work.

scenes.headline: DESIRE TO DEPLOY IS NOT READINESS
scenes.body: READINESS IS THE ABILITY TO OPERATE THE CONTROLS—NOT THE DESIRE TO DEPLOY.

builds.title: Messy Data Trust X-Ray
builds.final: MESSY DATA CAN SUPPORT A DECISION ONLY WHEN ITS LIMITS REMAIN VISIBLE.

scenes.headline: A CLEAN TABLE CAN HIDE A MESSY HISTORY
scenes.body: Completeness on screen does not prove the records are accurate, representative, current, or fit for this decision.

scenes.headline: TRACE WHERE EVERY FIELD CAME FROM
scenes.body: Keep source, collection method, transformation, timestamp, owner, and permitted use inspectable.

scenes.headline: TEST THE FAILURE MODES
scenes.body: Missingness, duplication, conflict, drift, outliers, and label uncertainty must remain separate signals.

scenes.headline: ASK WHO IS MISSING
scenes.body: Coverage can look large while systematically excluding people, places, outcomes, or hard-to-record cases.

scenes.headline: BOUND THE CLAIM AND THE USE
scenes.body: Name what the data can support, what it cannot support, the accountable reviewer, and the next verification action.

scenes.headline: DO NOT CLEAN AWAY THE WARNING
scenes.body: MESSY DATA CAN SUPPORT A DECISION ONLY WHEN ITS LIMITS REMAIN VISIBLE.

builds.title: Creator Ownership Stack Mapper
builds.final: PLATFORM REACH IS RENTED. YOUR OWNERSHIP STACK MUST SURVIVE THE PLATFORM.

scenes.headline: POSTING IS NOT OWNERSHIP
scenes.body: A platform can distribute the work without giving you control of the audience, archive, identity, or future access.

scenes.headline: NAME WHAT YOU ACTUALLY OWN
scenes.body: Track source files, authorship, licenses, collaborators, permissions, registrations, and every reused component.

scenes.headline: BUILD A DIRECT RELATIONSHIP
scenes.body: Consent-based email, portable contacts, preference history, and clear unsubscribe routes survive an algorithm change.

scenes.headline: KEEP THE CANONICAL COPY
scenes.body: Use your domain, durable archive, structured metadata, exports, backups, and migration paths as the source of truth.

scenes.headline: LET PLATFORMS BE CHANNELS
scenes.body: Syndicate outward, measure dependencies, preserve attribution, and keep a tested exit for every critical service.

scenes.headline: REACH IS NOT CONTROL
scenes.body: PLATFORM REACH IS RENTED. YOUR OWNERSHIP STACK MUST SURVIVE THE PLATFORM.

builds.title: Finding Is Part of Knowing
builds.final: KNOWLEDGE YOU CANNOT RELIABLY FIND IS KNOWLEDGE YOU CANNOT RELIABLY USE.

scenes.headline: STORED IS NOT FOUND
scenes.body: A fact can exist in the archive and still fail the person who needs it at the moment of decision.

scenes.headline: START WITH THE QUESTION
scenes.body: Model the language people actually use, the task they are doing, and the consequence of retrieving the wrong thing.

scenes.headline: GIVE KNOWLEDGE MORE THAN A TITLE
scenes.body: Stable identity, relationships, provenance, dates, audiences, and status make retrieval inspectable.

scenes.headline: RANK RELEVANCE WITH AUTHORITY
scenes.body: Similarity alone is not enough. Preserve source quality, freshness, scope, contradiction, and uncertainty.

scenes.headline: TEST WHAT PEOPLE CAN ACTUALLY FIND
scenes.body: Use known questions, missed results, false confidence, correction paths, and human feedback to measure the system.

scenes.headline: FINDING IS PART OF KNOWING
scenes.body: KNOWLEDGE YOU CANNOT RELIABLY FIND IS KNOWLEDGE YOU CANNOT RELIABLY USE.

builds.title: Change & Consequence Explorer
builds.final: A CHANGE IS NOT SMALL WHEN ITS CONSEQUENCES TRAVEL FARTHER THAN ITS AUTHOR CAN SEE.

scenes.headline: EVERY CHANGE ENTERS A SYSTEM
scenes.body: A policy edit, model update, data field, or workflow shortcut can alter outcomes far beyond the place it began.

scenes.headline: NAME WHAT WILL BE DIFFERENT
scenes.body: Record the actor, object, purpose, timing, assumptions, dependencies, and the prior state being replaced.

scenes.headline: FOLLOW WHO AND WHAT IT CAN REACH
scenes.body: Map direct effects, downstream handoffs, delayed effects, feedback loops, rights, and people carrying the burden.

scenes.headline: EXPECTED · EDGE · FAILURE · MISUSE
scenes.body: Compare evidence, uncertainty, reversibility, scale, severity, and the conditions that would change the conclusion.

scenes.headline: OWNER · MONITOR · STOP · REMEDY
scenes.body: A release needs accountable authority, observable signals, rollback criteria, notice, correction, and recourse.

scenes.headline: FOLLOW THE CONSEQUENCE PAST THE CHANGE
scenes.body: A CHANGE IS NOT SMALL WHEN ITS CONSEQUENCES TRAVEL FARTHER THAN ITS AUTHOR CAN SEE.

builds.title: Inclusive Experience Simulator & Repair Lab
builds.final: ACCESSIBILITY IS NOT A VIEW OF THE INTERFACE. IT IS WHETHER PEOPLE CAN COMPLETE THE WORK.

scenes.headline: PASSING A CHECKLIST IS NOT AN INCLUSIVE EXPERIENCE
scenes.body: A screen can satisfy isolated rules while real people still cannot perceive, understand, navigate, recover, or finish.

scenes.headline: TEST THE WHOLE JOURNEY
scenes.body: Follow entry, orientation, action, feedback, error, recovery, completion, and the handoff beyond the interface.

scenes.headline: VISION · HEARING · MOTOR · COGNITIVE · SPEECH
scenes.body: Add device, bandwidth, language, stress, interruption, assistive technology, and combinations of access needs.

scenes.headline: NAME WHERE THE TASK BREAKS
scenes.body: Record the affected person, blocked action, evidence, consequence, workaround, owner, and severity without impersonating lived experience.

scenes.headline: FIX THE SYSTEM—NOT THE PERSON
scenes.body: Change structure, language, control, feedback, timing, alternatives, and support; then rerun the same task and preserve the result.

scenes.headline: ACCESS MEANS COMPLETING THE WORK
scenes.body: ACCESSIBILITY IS NOT A VIEW OF THE INTERFACE. IT IS WHETHER PEOPLE CAN COMPLETE THE WORK.

builds.title: Privacy-Conscious Product Behavior X-Ray
builds.final: PRIVACY IS WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES WHEN NOBODY IS READING THE POLICY.

scenes.headline: A PRIVACY POLICY IS NOT PRODUCT BEHAVIOR
scenes.body: The real privacy posture appears in defaults, data flows, permissions, retention, inference, sharing, deletion, and failure states.

scenes.headline: TRACE DATA FROM ENTRY TO EXIT
scenes.body: Map collection, purpose, transformation, storage, access, disclosure, reuse, model input, retention, and verified deletion.

scenes.headline: WHAT HAPPENS BEFORE A PERSON CHOOSES?
scenes.body: Optional collection, tracking, sharing, personalization, and sensitive inference should not quietly activate through design or fatigue.

scenes.headline: CLAIM · CONTROL · EVIDENCE · RESULT
scenes.body: Test whether notice matches runtime behavior, the control changes processing, and the outcome remains visible and correctable.

scenes.headline: ACCESS · CORRECT · WITHDRAW · DELETE · APPEAL
scenes.body: Every route needs an owner, deadline, identity safeguards, downstream handling, exception basis, status, and escalation.

scenes.headline: READ THE PRODUCT THROUGH ITS BEHAVIOR
scenes.body: PRIVACY IS WHAT THE PRODUCT DOES WHEN NOBODY IS READING THE POLICY.

builds.title: Consequential AI Release Readiness Harness
builds.final: A RELEASE IS READY ONLY WHEN THE CONTROLS ARE OPERABLE, EVIDENCED, AND OWNED.

scenes.headline: A PASSING SCORE DOES NOT AUTHORIZE RELEASE
scenes.body: Consequential AI needs inspectable evidence that the use, workflow, people, vendor, data, and operating controls can hold under pressure.

scenes.headline: NAME THE VERSION AND THE CONSEQUENCE
scenes.body: Lock the model, data, configuration, purpose, affected people, decision, environment, change set, and unacceptable outcomes.

scenes.headline: EVIDENCE · CONTROL · OWNER · AUTHORITY
scenes.body: Test performance, workflow, privacy, security, accessibility, notice, review, appeal, incident response, monitoring, and rollback.

scenes.headline: EXPECTED · EDGE · MISUSE · OUTAGE
scenes.body: Use predeclared scenarios, thresholds, evidence locators, unresolved gaps, and independent challenge—not a launch-day demonstration.

scenes.headline: HOLD · REMEDIATE · PILOT · RELEASE · ROLLBACK
scenes.body: Record who can decide, what conditions apply, when the decision expires, what will be monitored, and what automatically stops the use.

scenes.headline: READINESS MUST SURVIVE CONTACT WITH OPERATIONS
scenes.body: A RELEASE IS READY ONLY WHEN THE CONTROLS ARE OPERABLE, EVIDENCED, AND OWNED.

builds.title: Adversarial System Explorer
builds.final: ADVERSARIAL TESTING IS USEFUL ONLY WHEN IT MAKES THE SYSTEM SAFER WITHOUT MAKING HARM EASIER.

scenes.headline: TEST THE SYSTEM WITHOUT TEACHING THE ATTACK
scenes.body: Defensive exploration should expose weak assumptions, controls, and recovery paths while withholding reusable harmful instructions.

scenes.headline: ASSET · THREAT · SCOPE · AUTHORITY
scenes.body: Name what is protected, the permitted environment, synthetic inputs, accountable owner, stop conditions, and prohibited actions.

scenes.headline: PRESSURE THE CONTROL—NOT REAL PEOPLE
scenes.body: Use abstract scenarios for misuse, manipulation, leakage, privilege, evasion, dependency failure, and unsafe automation.

scenes.headline: ISOLATE · MINIMIZE · MONITOR · STOP
scenes.body: Keep production data, credentials, live targets, personal information, and uncontrolled external effects outside the exercise.

scenes.headline: DETECT · REPAIR · RETEST · RECORD
scenes.body: Assign severity, evidence, owner, deadline, mitigation, rollback, verification, disclosure route, and residual risk.

scenes.headline: MAKE THE SYSTEM SAFER—NOT HARM EASIER
scenes.body: ADVERSARIAL TESTING IS USEFUL ONLY WHEN IT MAKES THE SYSTEM SAFER WITHOUT MAKING HARM EASIER.

builds.title: AI Failure & Incident Reconstruction Lab
builds.final: AN INCIDENT IS NOT CLOSED UNTIL THE EVIDENCE, CONSEQUENCE, CORRECTION, AND PREVENTION PATH ARE RECONSTRUCTABLE.

scenes.headline: THE FAILURE IS MORE THAN THE ERROR MESSAGE
scenes.body: An AI incident includes what happened, who was affected, how the workflow responded, what evidence survived, and whether harm can recur.

scenes.headline: FREEZE THE EVIDENCE WITHOUT COPYING THE HARM
scenes.body: Record time, version, configuration, inputs, outputs, decisions, actions, owners, and provenance while minimizing personal and sensitive data.

scenes.headline: EVENT · HANDOFF · CONTROL · CONSEQUENCE
scenes.body: Separate observed fact from inference. Trace chronology, dependencies, human actions, missing records, contradictions, and alternative explanations.

scenes.headline: NOTICE · STOP · CORRECT · REMEDY
scenes.body: Contain ongoing impact, preserve appeal and support routes, communicate uncertainty, and assign accountable deadlines.

scenes.headline: CAUSE · CONTROL · OWNER · RETEST
scenes.body: Distinguish root, contributing, and detection failures; change the system, verify the repair, monitor residual risk, and define rollback.

scenes.headline: RECONSTRUCTION MUST LEAD TO RECOURSE
scenes.body: AN INCIDENT IS NOT CLOSED UNTIL THE EVIDENCE, CONSEQUENCE, CORRECTION, AND PREVENTION PATH ARE RECONSTRUCTABLE.

builds.title: Data Exit & Portability Test
builds.final: DATA IS NOT PORTABLE UNTIL A PERSON CAN LEAVE WITH A COMPLETE, USABLE, AND SAFE COPY.

scenes.headline: AN EXPORT BUTTON IS NOT AN EXIT
scenes.body: Portability fails when the copy is incomplete, unreadable, undocumented, insecure, delayed, or impossible to use somewhere else.

scenes.headline: WHAT MUST LEAVE WITH THE PERSON?
scenes.body: Map account data, content, relationships, settings, consent history, provenance, derived records, media, and lawful exclusions.

scenes.headline: REQUEST · VERIFY · PREPARE · DELIVER
scenes.body: Test identity safeguards, status, deadline, secure transfer, expiry, retry, failure notice, support, and an auditable event record.

scenes.headline: COMPLETE · STRUCTURED · DOCUMENTED · USABLE
scenes.body: Check counts, checksums, schema, timestamps, encodings, relationships, metadata, accessibility, and import into an independent test environment.

scenes.headline: REVOKE · DELETE · RETAIN · CONFIRM
scenes.body: Separate portable data from lawful retention, stop future processing where required, handle downstream copies, and preserve appeal and correction routes.

scenes.headline: PORTABILITY MEANS A REAL WAY OUT
scenes.body: DATA IS NOT PORTABLE UNTIL A PERSON CAN LEAVE WITH A COMPLETE, USABLE, AND SAFE COPY.

builds.title: Resilience Mode / Offline Survival Test
builds.final: RESILIENCE IS NOT STAYING ONLINE. IT IS FAILING SAFELY AND RECOVERING TRUTHFULLY.

scenes.headline: OFFLINE IS A PRODUCT STATE—NOT AN ERROR PAGE
scenes.body: Essential work needs a deliberate mode for disconnection, partial service, stale data, queued actions, conflict, and recovery.

scenes.headline: WHAT MUST STILL BE POSSIBLE?
scenes.body: Name critical tasks, minimum evidence, local data, prohibited actions, human fallback, expiry, dependencies, and the consequence of delay.

scenes.headline: DETECT · EXPLAIN · LIMIT · CONTINUE
scenes.body: Make network state, freshness, unavailable features, safe capabilities, queued work, support, and stop conditions explicit.

scenes.headline: MINIMIZE · ENCRYPT · VERSION · EXPIRE
scenes.body: Store only what is necessary, preserve provenance and accessibility, prevent silent overwrite, and make device loss and shared-device risk visible.

scenes.headline: RECONNECT · COMPARE · RESOLVE · CONFIRM
scenes.body: Revalidate identity and freshness, detect conflicts and duplicates, require accountable resolution, sync safely, and record the resulting state.

scenes.headline: FAIL SAFELY. RECOVER TRUTHFULLY.
scenes.body: RESILIENCE IS NOT STAYING ONLINE. IT IS FAILING SAFELY AND RECOVERING TRUTHFULLY.

builds.title: Feedback → Change Governance Lab
builds.final: FEEDBACK BECOMES LEARNING ONLY THROUGH AN ACCOUNTABLE PATH FROM SIGNAL TO VERIFIED CHANGE.

scenes.headline: FEEDBACK IS A SIGNAL—NOT A PRODUCT COMMAND
scenes.body: A comment can reveal correction, outcome, unmet need, misuse, access barrier, or preference without proving what should change.

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · CONSENT · MINIMIZATION · PROVENANCE
scenes.body: Use synthetic reporting in the lab. Separate content from identity, protect sensitive detail, preserve context, and offer correction and withdrawal routes.

scenes.headline: EVIDENCE · RECURRENCE · CONSEQUENCE · UNCERTAINTY
scenes.body: Deduplicate carefully, keep minority and contradictory reports visible, test source limits, and route urgent harm to accountable human triage.

scenes.headline: PROPOSAL · OWNER · AUTHORITY · DECISION
scenes.body: Link the feedback to a bounded change, alternatives, affected people, evidence, risks, dependencies, approval, dissent, conditions, and rollback.

scenes.headline: VALIDATE · COMMUNICATE · MONITOR · CORRECT
scenes.body: Test whether the change works, tell reporters what happened when appropriate, watch intended and unintended outcomes, and preserve the record.

scenes.headline: SIGNAL → DECISION → VERIFIED CHANGE
scenes.body: FEEDBACK BECOMES LEARNING ONLY THROUGH AN ACCOUNTABLE PATH FROM SIGNAL TO VERIFIED CHANGE.

builds.title: Domain AI Evaluation Studio
builds.final: A DOMAIN EVALUATION SUPPORTS ONLY THE USE, DATA, CONDITIONS, AND CONSEQUENCES IT ACTUALLY TESTED.

scenes.headline: A BENCHMARK SCORE IS NOT GENERAL PERFORMANCE
scenes.body: A model can look strong on synthetic examples and still fail the domain, workflow, people, conditions, or consequence that matter.

scenes.headline: NAME THE USE AND THE DECISION
scenes.body: Lock model and version, domain task, population, environment, human role, success criteria, unacceptable outcomes, and what the test cannot prove.

scenes.headline: REPRESENTATIVE · EDGE · FAILURE · ABSTAIN
scenes.body: Use synthetic cases with provenance, coverage rationale, protected challenge sets, known limitations, and competent domain review.

scenes.headline: QUALITY · SAFETY · FAIRNESS · RELIABILITY
scenes.body: Keep uncertainty, subgroup behavior, calibration, refusals, consistency, latency, cost, and human-workflow effects visible instead of one average.

scenes.headline: EVIDENCE · LIMIT · OWNER · NEXT TEST
scenes.body: Preserve errors and contradictions, investigate causes, compare alternatives, define monitoring and stops, and never let the score approve deployment.

scenes.headline: THE CLAIM CANNOT OUTRUN THE TEST
scenes.body: A DOMAIN EVALUATION SUPPORTS ONLY THE USE, DATA, CONDITIONS, AND CONSEQUENCES IT ACTUALLY TESTED.

builds.title: Agent Work Trace Inspector
builds.final: ACCOUNTABLE AGENT WORK LEAVES AN INSPECTABLE TRAIL WITHOUT EXPOSING PRIVATE CONTENT.

scenes.headline: A TRACE IS EVIDENCE—NOT THE TRUTH
scenes.body: An event log can show sequence and state without proving intent, correctness, completeness, causation, or a safe outcome.

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · AUTHORITY · SCOPE · STOP
scenes.body: Lock agent and model version, environment, permitted tools and data, accountable owner, approval gates, prohibited actions, and termination conditions.

scenes.headline: EVENT · TIME · STATE · RESULT
scenes.body: Use synthetic redacted traces. Record requests, tool outcomes, approvals, errors, retries, and side effects—never credentials, secrets, or private content.

scenes.headline: OBSERVED ≠ INFERRED ≠ VERIFIED
scenes.body: Preserve provenance, missing events, uncertainty, contradictions, transformations, and reviewer notes instead of inventing a continuous story.

scenes.headline: REPLAY · CONTAIN · CORRECT · VALIDATE
scenes.body: Check permissions, sequence, human intervention, external change, stop behavior, and consequence before deciding whether work can stand.

scenes.headline: INSPECTABLE WITHOUT EXPOSURE
scenes.body: ACCOUNTABLE AGENT WORK LEAVES AN INSPECTABLE TRAIL WITHOUT EXPOSING PRIVATE CONTENT.

builds.title: AI Stop / Escalate Engine
builds.final: A SAFE BOUNDARY MAKES CONTINUE, ASK, ABSTAIN, FALL BACK, ESCALATE, AND STOP EXPLICIT.

scenes.headline: CONFIDENCE IS NOT PERMISSION TO CONTINUE
scenes.body: A fluent answer can conceal missing evidence, failed tools, high consequence, or uncertainty that should change the next action.

scenes.headline: CONSEQUENCE · EVIDENCE · UNCERTAINTY
scenes.body: Use a dated versioned policy. Name required controls, accountable humans, tool dependencies, verified fallbacks, and expiry before selecting an action.

scenes.headline: CONTINUE · ASK · ABSTAIN
scenes.body: Continue only inside the declared boundary. Ask when evidence can be repaired. Abstain when the model lacks a safe or authorized path.

scenes.headline: FALL BACK · ESCALATE · STOP
scenes.body: Require a verified fallback after a required tool fails. Escalate high-consequence uncertainty. Stop when neither control is available.

scenes.headline: TIME PRESSURE NEVER LOWERS THE GATE
scenes.body: Preserve the rule, reason, blockers, inherited control records, and exact state-only replay without invoking tools or repeating side effects.

scenes.headline: MAKE THE NEXT ACTION EXPLICIT
scenes.body: A SAFE BOUNDARY MAKES CONTINUE, ASK, ABSTAIN, FALL BACK, ESCALATE, AND STOP EXPLICIT.

builds.title: Who Owns the AI Work?
builds.final: ACCOUNTABILITY BEGINS WHEN EVERY AI TOOL, DECISION, VENDOR, AND WORKFLOW HAS A VISIBLE OWNER.

scenes.headline: AI WORK CAN EXIST WITHOUT AN OWNER
scenes.body: A tool can enter a workflow, influence a decision, or depend on a vendor while responsibility remains assumed, fragmented, or invisible.

scenes.headline: TOOL · DECISION · VENDOR · WORKFLOW
scenes.body: Use synthetic records to connect each AI component to its purpose, accountable role, approving authority, operator, affected workflow, and review date.

scenes.headline: NO OWNER · STALE OWNER · SPLIT AUTHORITY
scenes.body: Flag missing assignments, departed owners, conflicting roles, expired reviews, unowned vendor changes, and decisions nobody is authorized to make.

scenes.headline: FROM · TO · AUTHORITY · EFFECTIVE DATE
scenes.body: A reassignment must preserve the prior owner, reason, approval, scope, evidence, effective time, open duties, and a path to challenge or correct it.

scenes.headline: A MAP IS NOT ACCOUNTABILITY
scenes.body: Visible assignments do not prove oversight, competence, compliance, safety, performance, or that the named person accepted and exercised the role.

scenes.headline: MAKE OWNERSHIP VISIBLE
scenes.body: ACCOUNTABILITY BEGINS WHEN EVERY AI TOOL, DECISION, VENDOR, AND WORKFLOW HAS A VISIBLE OWNER.

builds.title: Give the AI a Real Job
builds.final: AN AI AGENT HAS A REAL JOB ONLY WHEN ITS ROLE, TOOLS, BOUNDARIES, REVIEW POINTS, AND STOP CONDITIONS ARE EXPLICIT.

scenes.headline: A PROMPT IS NOT A JOB DESCRIPTION
scenes.body: An agent can produce fluent work while its purpose, authority, tools, accountable owner, prohibited actions, and required review remain undefined.

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · INPUT · OUTPUT · OWNER
scenes.body: Use a synthetic role to name the bounded task, accepted inputs, expected artifact, responsible human, affected people, success criteria, and consequence.

scenes.headline: ALLOW · DENY · REQUIRE APPROVAL
scenes.body: Assign only necessary tools and data. Separate read, draft, recommend, communicate, transact, and delete permissions; attach evidence and expiry.

scenes.headline: PERMISSION · RISK · EVALUATION
scenes.body: When work moves in or out, recompute required access, consequence, evaluation coverage, human review, inherited ownership, and the safe fallback.

scenes.headline: REVIEW · ESCALATE · ABSTAIN · STOP
scenes.body: Require review before consequential action. Preserve uncertainty, failed tools, boundary violations, escalation routes, termination rules, and exact state-only replay.

scenes.headline: GIVE THE AGENT A REAL JOB
scenes.body: AN AI AGENT HAS A REAL JOB ONLY WHEN ITS ROLE, TOOLS, BOUNDARIES, REVIEW POINTS, AND STOP CONDITIONS ARE EXPLICIT.

builds.title: Design an AI Team
builds.final: AN AI TEAM IS GOVERNED ONLY WHEN EVERY HANDOFF PRESERVES PURPOSE, AUTHORITY, EVIDENCE, SUPERVISION, AND A SAFE FAILURE PATH.

scenes.headline: MORE AGENTS CREATE MORE HANDOFFS
scenes.body: Splitting complex work can add specialization while multiplying lost context, duplicated effort, hidden permissions, coordination cost, and unowned failure.

scenes.headline: ROLE · OWNER · INPUT · OUTPUT
scenes.body: Use a synthetic topology to bind each agent and person to a bounded job, accountable owner, permitted tools, evidence contract, review point, and stop rule.

scenes.headline: SOURCE · TRANSFORM · RECEIVER · ACCEPTANCE
scenes.body: Pass the smallest necessary state. Preserve provenance, uncertainty, constraints, rejected work, authority, expected response, and proof that the receiver accepted it.

scenes.headline: BOTTLENECK · SUPERVISION · COST · FAILURE
scenes.body: When a role or connection changes, recalculate queue pressure, human review, access, latency, spend, evaluation coverage, and every reachable failure path.

scenes.headline: CONTAIN · FALL BACK · ESCALATE · STOP
scenes.body: Block loops, stale or conflicting state, unauthorized tools, missing owners, and failed required checks; preserve exact trace and accountable human intervention.

scenes.headline: CONTROL LIVES BETWEEN THE NODES
scenes.body: AN AI TEAM IS GOVERNED ONLY WHEN EVERY HANDOFF PRESERVES PURPOSE, AUTHORITY, EVIDENCE, SUPERVISION, AND A SAFE FAILURE PATH.

builds.title: Reuse the Parts That Regulation Keeps Requiring
builds.final: REGULATED COMPONENTS ARE REUSABLE ONLY WHEN CONTEXT, EVIDENCE, AUTHORITY, VERSION, AND INVALIDATION TRAVEL WITH THEM.

scenes.headline: RECURRING REQUIREMENTS ARE NOT COPY-PASTE BLOCKS
scenes.body: Approvals, consent, evidence, disclosures, and records recur, but the rule, actor, purpose, jurisdiction, risk, and effective date can change what is valid.

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · INPUT · OUTPUT · OWNER
scenes.body: Use synthetic records to bind each component to authority, evidence, required fields, accountable role, review gate, version, effective period, and prohibited reuse.

scenes.headline: APPROVE · CONSENT · DISCLOSE · RECORD
scenes.body: Compose only compatible components. Preserve order, dependencies, decisions, signatures, provenance, retention, correction, withdrawal, and human review.

scenes.headline: ACTOR · USE · PLACE · CONSEQUENCE
scenes.body: When a declared condition changes, recompute applicability, required evidence, permissions, language, review, downstream records, and every affected component.

scenes.headline: STALE · CONFLICT · MISSING · REVOKED
scenes.body: Fail closed on expired authority, incompatible versions, missing evidence, revoked consent, broken dependencies, or context outside the component’s declared scope.

scenes.headline: REUSE THE CONTROL—NOT THE ASSUMPTION
scenes.body: REGULATED COMPONENTS ARE REUSABLE ONLY WHEN CONTEXT, EVIDENCE, AUTHORITY, VERSION, AND INVALIDATION TRAVEL WITH THEM.

builds.title: Cannabis Care Access Journey
builds.final: ACCESS IS THE WHOLE JOURNEY THROUGH INFORMATION, ELIGIBILITY, COST, TRAVEL, CLINICIANS, SUPPLY, AND CONTINUING CARE.

scenes.headline: AVAILABILITY IS NOT ACCESS
scenes.body: A program or product can exist while a person still cannot understand the rules, qualify, afford the process, reach care, find supply, or continue safely.

scenes.headline: LEARN · QUALIFY · PAY · TRAVEL
scenes.body: Use synthetic people and places to trace required information, eligibility, documents, fees, appointments, distance, time, mobility, language, privacy, and support.

scenes.headline: CLINICIAN · PRODUCT · SUPPLY · FOLLOW-UP
scenes.body: Keep clinical judgment human. Show availability, product and formulation constraints, pharmacy or dispensary steps, continuity, monitoring, and what remains unknown.

scenes.headline: COST · MOBILITY · ELIGIBILITY · LOCATION
scenes.body: When one constraint changes, reroute the declared path and recompute time, expense, travel, required steps, barriers, alternatives, and unresolved dead ends.

scenes.headline: A ROUTE IS NOT CARE OR LEGAL ADVICE
scenes.body: A modeled journey cannot verify current law, eligibility, clinical appropriateness, product safety, inventory, affordability, accessibility, or a successful outcome.

scenes.headline: MEASURE THE WHOLE JOURNEY
scenes.body: ACCESS IS THE WHOLE JOURNEY THROUGH INFORMATION, ELIGIBILITY, COST, TRAVEL, CLINICIANS, SUPPLY, AND CONTINUING CARE.

builds.title: What Does This Island Depend On?
builds.final: ISLAND RESILIENCE STARTS BY MAKING DEPENDENCIES, CASCADES, UNEQUAL CONSEQUENCES, AND RECOVERY CHOICES VISIBLE.

scenes.headline: ESSENTIAL SYSTEMS DO NOT END AT THE SHORE
scenes.body: Food, water, energy, health, communications, transport, waste, finance, and public services depend on linked local capacity and external routes.

scenes.headline: SOURCE · ROUTE · SERVICE · PLACE
scenes.body: Use synthetic infrastructure to connect each essential function to upstream supply, local assets, operators, alternatives, inventory, geography, and accountable owners.

scenes.headline: PORT · CABLE · ROUTE · SERVICE
scenes.body: Remove a declared node or edge and trace immediate loss, delayed effects, cross-sector cascades, geographic reach, duration, uncertainty, and evidence limits.

scenes.headline: ACCESS · HEALTH · COST · MOBILITY
scenes.body: Do not flatten island impact into one score. Preserve who is affected first, who has fewer substitutes, what burdens shift, and which communities define priority.

scenes.headline: FALL BACK · ALLOCATE · RESTORE · LEARN
scenes.body: Compare bounded alternatives, prerequisites, tradeoffs, human authority, stop rules, restoration sequence, residual risk, and changes required before the next disruption.

scenes.headline: SEE THE SYSTEM BEFORE IT BREAKS
scenes.body: ISLAND RESILIENCE STARTS BY MAKING DEPENDENCIES, CASCADES, UNEQUAL CONSEQUENCES, AND RECOVERY CHOICES VISIBLE.

builds.title: Will This Work Here?
builds.final: TRANSFERABILITY MUST BE EARNED BY TESTING THE INTERVENTION AGAINST THE PLACE, ITS PEOPLE, AND ITS DEPENDENCIES.

scenes.headline: A GOOD IDEA DOES NOT ARRIVE CONTEXT-FREE
scenes.body: A policy, technology, service, or program can succeed somewhere else and still fail when assumptions about people, place, infrastructure, authority, and resources change.

scenes.headline: PURPOSE · INPUT · WORKFORCE · COST
scenes.body: Use synthetic profiles to bind the intervention to its intended outcome, evidence, language, staffing, funding, technology, delivery model, dependencies, and nonnegotiable limits.

scenes.headline: ACCESS · CAPACITY · CULTURE · INFRASTRUCTURE
scenes.body: Compare declared conditions without ranking communities. Expose missing workforce, connectivity, language, mobility, institutional support, local knowledge, and community authority.

scenes.headline: KEEP · ADAPT · BUILD CAPACITY · STOP
scenes.body: When the place changes, recompute every gap and required adaptation. Preserve uncertainty, evidence limits, affected people, tradeoffs, ownership, and conditions that block transfer.

scenes.headline: A SCORE IS NOT FEASIBILITY OR CONSENT
scenes.body: A synthetic match cannot establish effectiveness, legality, safety, funding, procurement readiness, community acceptance, implementation capacity, or permission to proceed.

scenes.headline: MAKE TRANSFERABILITY EARN ITS NAME
scenes.body: TRANSFERABILITY MUST BE EARNED BY TESTING THE INTERVENTION AGAINST THE PLACE, ITS PEOPLE, AND ITS DEPENDENCIES.

builds.title: What Does This Rule Feel Like in Real Life?
builds.final: A RULE IS NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD UNTIL ITS PROCEDURE, BURDEN, EXPERIENCE, AND RECOURSE CAN BE READ TOGETHER.

scenes.headline: THE RULE AND THE JOURNEY ARE NOT THE SAME RECORD
scenes.body: Formal language can describe eligibility, duties, steps, and remedies while hiding the time, cost, uncertainty, exposure, and effort required to navigate them.

scenes.headline: AUTHORITY · STEP · DECISION · RECOURSE
scenes.body: Use a dated synthetic rule to map who acts, what is required, which evidence counts, where discretion enters, what notice is given, and how a decision can be challenged.

scenes.headline: TIME · COST · ACCESS · CONSEQUENCE
scenes.body: Use synthetic experiences to preserve actual sequence, waiting, travel, language, disability, privacy, confusion, failed attempts, support, and unequal burden without claiming representativeness.

scenes.headline: PROPAGATE THE EFFECT
scenes.body: When a step, document, deadline, channel, decision point, or recourse changes, recompute burden, access, failure points, notice, evidence, and downstream consequences.

scenes.headline: TEXT ≠ PRACTICE ≠ EXPERIENCE
scenes.body: One rule, modeled path, or account cannot prove implementation, prevalence, fairness, causation, legal interpretation, remedy, or what every person experiences.

scenes.headline: READ THE RULE WITH THE JOURNEY
scenes.body: A RULE IS NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD UNTIL ITS PROCEDURE, BURDEN, EXPERIENCE, AND RECOURSE CAN BE READ TOGETHER.

builds.title: What Works for You?
builds.final: PERSONAL CONTEXT BECOMES USEFUL WHEN IT STAYS PRIVATE, CORRECTABLE, SITUATIONAL, AND OWNED BY THE PERSON IT DESCRIBES.

scenes.headline: A PREFERENCE IS NOT A PERMANENT TRAIT
scenes.body: What helps or overwhelms a person can change with setting, goal, health, energy, company, timing, access, and prior response.

scenes.headline: PREFERENCE · SENSITIVITY · GOAL · RESPONSE
scenes.body: Use synthetic browser-local records. Collect only what the person chooses, name purpose and expiry, preserve source and uncertainty, and offer correction, deletion, and export.

scenes.headline: SETTING · TIME · SUPPORT · CONSTRAINT
scenes.body: Bind each response to the conditions in which it occurred. Keep contradictions, unknowns, changes, and one-off experiences instead of flattening them into a fixed profile.

scenes.headline: REORGANIZE—DO NOT DIAGNOSE
scenes.body: When setting, goals, sensitivities, or responses change, reorder the visible constellation without inferring identity, disability, health status, intent, or what will work next.

scenes.headline: VIEW · CORRECT · WITHDRAW · EXIT
scenes.body: Let the person inspect every field, restrict reuse and sharing, revoke consent, delete local state, carry a portable record, and choose no recommendation.

scenes.headline: CONTEXT BELONGS TO THE PERSON
scenes.body: PERSONAL CONTEXT BECOMES USEFUL WHEN IT STAYS PRIVATE, CORRECTABLE, SITUATIONAL, AND OWNED BY THE PERSON IT DESCRIBES.

builds.title: How Is This Space Affecting You?
builds.final: A SPACE BECOMES LEGIBLE WHEN CONDITIONS, EXPERIENCE, EVIDENCE STRENGTH, AND TRADEOFFS CAN BE READ TOGETHER.

scenes.headline: A ROOM IS NOT A NEUTRAL CONTAINER
scenes.body: Light, sound, layout, temperature, nature, crowding, timing, task, and control may shape experience—but the same condition does not affect every person or goal the same way.

scenes.headline: LIGHT · SOUND · LAYOUT · NATURE
scenes.body: Use exact-bound synthetic rooms. Keep each feature visible with setting, goal, duration, available control, uncertainty, and what has not actually been measured.

scenes.headline: THE INTERPRETATION MUST MOVE
scenes.body: When a room or goal changes, recompute only the declared model. Preserve competing needs, interactions, unknowns, and the possibility that one feature helps one goal while complicating another.

scenes.headline: MODERATE · LIMITED · UNKNOWN
scenes.body: An evidence label must expose scope and uncertainty. It cannot turn an illustrative model, association, preference, or single experience into a causal or universal conclusion.

scenes.headline: MODEL ≠ MEASUREMENT ≠ PRESCRIPTION
scenes.body: A synthetic load cannot diagnose harm, measure exposure, prove causation, determine accessibility or compliance, represent every person, or prescribe a real design.

scenes.headline: READ THE ROOM WITH THE PERSON
scenes.body: A SPACE BECOMES LEGIBLE WHEN CONDITIONS, EXPERIENCE, EVIDENCE STRENGTH, AND TRADEOFFS CAN BE READ TOGETHER.

builds.title: Teach Me the Cannabis Part I Actually Need
builds.final: THE RIGHT LESSON STARTS WITH THE QUESTION, PRESERVES UNCERTAINTY, AND STOPS WHERE EDUCATION BECOMES PERSONAL ADVICE.

scenes.headline: ONE GENERIC CANNABIS LESSON IS NOT ENOUGH
scenes.body: A question about basics, evidence, products, risk, or law begins in a different place—but personalization must not become medical or legal advice.

scenes.headline: QUESTION · EXPERIENCE · MISCONCEPTION
scenes.body: Use an exact-bound synthetic learner. Keep jurisdiction and risk explicit, collect no real health profile, and preserve what the learner has not said.

scenes.headline: ORDER · DEPTH · CHECK · CORRECT
scenes.body: Adapt only the curriculum sequence and knowledge checks. Show dated authoritative evidence, its limits, and the difference between association and causation.

scenes.headline: ESCALATE · CHECK CURRENT LAW
scenes.body: Pregnancy, youth, poisoning, driving, interactions, severe symptoms, and legal questions route to current authoritative or professional help—not a personalized answer.

scenes.headline: EDUCATION IS NOT CLEARANCE
scenes.body: The demo cannot diagnose, treat, recommend cannabis, choose a product or dose, predict impairment, establish safety, or state that a dated source answers every jurisdiction.

scenes.headline: TEACH THE PART THAT FITS
scenes.body: THE RIGHT LESSON STARTS WITH THE QUESTION, PRESERVES UNCERTAINTY, AND STOPS WHERE EDUCATION BECOMES PERSONAL ADVICE.

builds.title: Beyond the Strain Name
builds.final: A NAME CANNOT CARRY COMPOSITION, FORMAT, CONTEXT, UNCERTAINTY, OR A PERSON'S GOALS.

scenes.headline: A STRAIN NAME IS NOT A PRODUCT MODEL
scenes.body: The same or similar label can conceal different formats, declared composition, batches, evidence, contexts, and unknowns.

scenes.headline: COMPOSITION · FORMAT · CONTEXT
scenes.body: Use exact-bound synthetic products and relative bands. Keep label, goal, constraints, missing evidence, and NOT COLLECTED person context visible.

scenes.headline: LET THE DIMENSIONS REORGANIZE
scenes.body: When the learning goal or comparison pair changes, reorganize only the visible dimensions. Do not turn similarity into equivalence, effect, quality, or fit.

scenes.headline: DECLARED · SYNTHETIC · UNKNOWN
scenes.body: A displayed band is not a dose, potency result, laboratory analysis, verified label, batch record, predicted experience, or current legal status.

scenes.headline: COMPARE—DO NOT RECOMMEND
scenes.body: The demo cannot rank products, match one to a person, predict effects, guide purchase or use, interpret a certificate, or establish safety, legality, or effectiveness.

scenes.headline: LOOK BEYOND THE NAME
scenes.body: A NAME CANNOT CARRY COMPOSITION, FORMAT, CONTEXT, UNCERTAINTY, OR A PERSON'S GOALS.

builds.title: Run a Tiny Experiment on Your Own Environment
builds.final: A TINY EXPERIMENT BECOMES USEFUL WHEN THE PROTOCOL MAKES ALTERNATIVES, REPETITION, CONFOUNDING, AND UNCERTAINTY VISIBLE.

scenes.headline: ONE DIFFERENT DAY IS NOT AN EXPERIMENT
scenes.body: A change in light, sound, layout, nature, timing, task, or expectation can move with the outcome and make a simple before-and-after story misleading.

scenes.headline: CONDITION · SEQUENCE · MEASURE · STOP
scenes.body: Use an exact-bound synthetic protocol. Name the comparison, repeated observations, timing, confounders, missing data, human control, and conditions that end the test.

scenes.headline: ALTERNATE · REPEAT · UNBLOCK
scenes.body: Replace a blocked, confounded sequence with a longer alternating one. Recompute only descriptive condition means, their difference, and declared design features.

scenes.headline: WEAK · LIMITED · PATTERN TO RETEST
scenes.body: Strength reflects sequence, repetition, and confounding—not an effect, causal conclusion, health measure, universal response, or proof the environment produced change.

scenes.headline: DESCRIPTION IS NOT PRESCRIPTION
scenes.body: The demo cannot conduct research, diagnose, treat, measure cognition or exposure, determine safety or accessibility, infer a population effect, or recommend a real environmental change.

scenes.headline: MAKE THE PROTOCOL VISIBLE
scenes.body: A TINY EXPERIMENT BECOMES USEFUL WHEN THE PROTOCOL MAKES ALTERNATIVES, REPETITION, CONFOUNDING, AND UNCERTAINTY VISIBLE.

builds.title: Make the Space Adapt to the Person
builds.final: AN ADAPTIVE SPACE IS ACCOUNTABLE ONLY WHEN PROPOSALS, TRADEOFFS, AUTHORITY, CONSENT, OVERRIDE, AND FALLBACK REMAIN VISIBLE.

scenes.headline: A ROOM CAN ADAPT WITHOUT DECIDING FOR A PERSON
scenes.body: Light, quiet zones, and seating can be proposed from a synthetic task and context—but a configuration is not permission to change a real space.

scenes.headline: PERSON · TASK · CONTEXT · CONSTRAINT
scenes.body: Use only an exact-bound synthetic scenario. Keep occupants, task, preferences, conflicts, unknowns, authority, and available controls visible.

scenes.headline: SETTING · RATIONALE · TRADEOFF
scenes.body: When the scenario changes, recompute proposed light, quiet-zone, and seating settings. Preserve unresolved conditions and explicit non-actions.

scenes.headline: ONE PERSON · MANY PEOPLE · HUMAN REVIEW
scenes.body: A setting that supports one task may complicate another. Do not collapse competing needs into a score, prediction, inferred trait, or automatic accommodation.

scenes.headline: PROPOSE—DO NOT ACTUATE
scenes.body: The demo reads no sensors, controls no equipment, measures no effect, infers no protected trait, and cannot determine safety, accessibility, compliance, or personal need.

scenes.headline: KEEP THE PERSON IN CONTROL
scenes.body: AN ADAPTIVE SPACE IS ACCOUNTABLE ONLY WHEN PROPOSALS, TRADEOFFS, AUTHORITY, CONSENT, OVERRIDE, AND FALLBACK REMAIN VISIBLE.

builds.title: Let the Smart Home Explain Itself
builds.final: A SMART ENVIRONMENT IS ACCOUNTABLE ONLY WHEN AUTHORITY, EXPLANATION, OVERRIDE, FAILURE, AND RECOVERY TRAVEL WITH EVERY STATE CHANGE.

scenes.headline: A SMART HOME ACTION NEEDS AN ACCOUNTABLE STORY
scenes.body: A synthetic environment can change state—but every proposed action still needs purpose, authority, explanation, override, and a recoverable prior state.

scenes.headline: TRIGGER · ACTION · AUTHORITY · LIMIT
scenes.body: Use exact-bound synthetic rooms and devices. Preserve who may authorize, affected occupants, prerequisites, conflicts, expiry, non-actions, and the safe default.

scenes.headline: BEFORE · CHANGE · REASON · AFTER
scenes.body: Advance state only inside the declared fixture. Record the rule, evidence, authorization, consequence, uncertainty, and an explanation a person can inspect.

scenes.headline: CONFLICT · OUTAGE · OVERRIDE · ROLLBACK
scenes.body: When authority conflicts or a dependency fails, do not continue silently. Pause, preserve state, expose the blocker, accept human override, and restore a known prior state.

scenes.headline: SIMULATION—NOT ACTUATION
scenes.body: No device or sensor is connected. The demo cannot infer authority or person traits, secure a home, determine safety or accessibility, decide an accommodation, or prove benefit.

scenes.headline: MAKE EVERY ACTION REVERSIBLE
scenes.body: A SMART ENVIRONMENT IS ACCOUNTABLE ONLY WHEN AUTHORITY, EXPLANATION, OVERRIDE, FAILURE, AND RECOVERY TRAVEL WITH EVERY STATE CHANGE.

builds.title: What Do You Actually Own That Others Cannot Easily Copy?
builds.final: DEFENSIBILITY BECOMES LEGIBLE WHEN CLAIMED ASSETS, RIGHTS, DEPENDENCIES, SUBSTITUTES, EVIDENCE, AND FAILURE PATHS CAN BE READ TOGETHER.

scenes.headline: A LIST OF ASSETS IS NOT A MOAT
scenes.body: Data, rights, relationships, workflows, trust, knowledge, and feedback may matter—but possession or access does not establish ownership, control, or durable advantage.

scenes.headline: ASSET · RIGHT · RELATIONSHIP · DEPENDENCY
scenes.body: Use an exact-bound synthetic organization. Connect each claimed asset to source, permission, control, replaceability, transfer limits, upkeep, evidence, and dependent capabilities.

scenes.headline: POSSESS · ACCESS · PERMISSION · CONTROL
scenes.body: Keep legal ownership separate from holding a copy, reaching a resource, receiving limited permission, or controlling a workflow. Name expiry, revocation, and uncertainty.

scenes.headline: WATCH THE TOPOLOGY CHANGE
scenes.body: Delete one illustrative node or edge and recompute only declared dependencies, substitutes, feedback paths, concentration, fragility, and what remains unsupported.

scenes.headline: A MAP IS NOT A VERDICT
scenes.body: The demo cannot determine title, ownership, IP rights, legality, valuation, investability, competitive advantage, durability, defensibility, or commercial success.

scenes.headline: TEST WHAT SURVIVES REMOVAL
scenes.body: DEFENSIBILITY BECOMES LEGIBLE WHEN CLAIMED ASSETS, RIGHTS, DEPENDENCIES, SUBSTITUTES, EVIDENCE, AND FAILURE PATHS CAN BE READ TOGETHER.
